name: 426. Passthrough extra params cannot add stream or another vendor's name for the model (extra-params-unsettable)
description: Folder 409 pins the rule that an extra param never replaces a field the request set. That rule reads the converted body, so it says nothing about a field the converter left out. Two kinds of such fields matter. A buffered converter leaves stream out: with extra_params.stream=true the vendor was asked to stream, billed the tokens, and the buffered path could not parse the event stream, so the caller got an error and no usage was recorded (measured against a local vendor; TestExtraParamsCannotSwitchStreaming). And some vendors read the model, or the deployment that stands for it, under a name other than model (model_id, version, deployment, deployment_id, engine): a converter that routes by URL leaves that name out of the body, where one added by an extra param could be read in the URL's place. providerUtils.MergeExtraParamsIntoJSON now refuses an extra param that would add one of these names to a body that lacks it, in any spelling, with 400 caller_invalid_request naming the extra param, before any upstream call; the form writers and Bedrock rerank refuse the same names. The list is one place for every provider (unsettableExtraParamFields). The first seven rows pin the refusal of the shared JSON merge on the /openai drop-in routes, buffered and streamed. The last six cover the paths that apply the rule on their own, one row each with the route's real ingress shape: the OpenAI transcription form on the native and the drop-in route, the ElevenLabs transcription form, the image edit form, Bedrock rerank, and Perplexity chat, whose converter used to read stream out of the extra params. The streamed row plants stream=false against the stream=true the request set, which is the replace case of folder 409 and is kept here beside its buffered twin.
